rename.to: declarative cols that have explicit name get placed at the top of the cols list above other attrs

body: I will fix this today for 2.0.  unfortunately zero chance of this being changed in 1.4.

Interesting, this applies only to the SELECT statement and not the Table itself.   OK, most of the hard work w/ the ordering is getting them from the class to the table, that's what people usually care about.  this is just the ORM assignment part of it.

rename.from: declarative cols that have explicit name get placed at the top of the cols list above other attrs
rename.to: declarative cols that have explicit name get placed at the top of the cols list above other attrs, within the mapper only, not the table which is OK

body: this is an old issue, does it in 1.3, probably been this way a long time.

> this applies only to the SELECT statement and not the Table itself. 

in this case in the 1.x series you can use as workaround `session.query(Styles.__table__)`

> > this applies only to the SELECT statement and not the Table itself.
> 
> in this case in the 1.x series you can use as workaround `session.query(Styles.__table__)`

that's probably not going to work beacuse those cols would not be ORM annotated.

I've identified this issue all the way at bedrock.  Minecraft level 2 where you're hitting the bottom of the game :)   it's not *too* hard to fix but the thing causing this to happen goes back to v0.0.1.      So.... :)   good timing that we are at 2.0 and can change something this fundamental.

> that's probably not going to work beacuse those cols would not be ORM annotated.

well, the use case is `pd.read_sql_query(session.query(TableClass), con)` so for that it should be fine

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **main** branch:

**reconcile Mapper properties ordering against mapped Table** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/4150

btw @demishu  this is a *great* improvement.  I have a lot of tests to update but they are all being adjusted so that SELECT statements render columns in table order regardless of config, which is great.   This seems to be your first bug report ever on github, you should get a badge for a very rare hole-in-one, getting the SQLAlchemy guy to like your suggestion, a change for something that's been the same way for decades, not a common occurrence :)
